```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Where a camera is deployed shapes what it can detect and how its data can be pooled with 
others. WildObsR places camera coordinates in their Australian context by describing a 
spatial hierarchy, beginning with the state or territory, then to the IBRA bioregion 
and subregion, then to the nearest protected area. WildObsR also offers tools to help with
metric map projection, and quickly determining the spacing between neighbouring cameras. 
The state, bioregion and protected-area layers ship with the package, so everything here 
runs offline. This vignette uses the two projects bundled with WildObsR, one from several
national parks in the Queensland Wet Tropics and one from Woomargama National Park in New
South Wales.

```{r data}
# load the R package
library(WildObsR)

# load the two projects shipped with WildObsR
dp_list <- example_datapackages()

# combine both deployments tables for both projects
deps <- do.call(rbind, lapply(dp_list, function(dp) {
  # this project's deployments, read with their schema types
  d <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "deployments")
  # subset the deployments to only include spatial information 
  d[, c("deploymentID", "locationID", "locationName", "latitude", "longitude")]
}))
# de-duplicate by removing the first duplicated locationID, 
# since one locationID can contain several cameras
stations <- deps[!duplicated(deps$locationID), ]
# remove row names and count how many rows
rownames(stations) <- NULL
# and count how many rows
nrow(stations)
```

## State or territory

The function `AUS_state_locator()` adds the state or territory each camera falls in, 
from the boundaries exported in the [`ozmaps`](https://mdsumner.github.io/ozmaps/) R 
package. State matters because threatened-species listings, and so the obscuring of
public records, differ between states.

```{r state}
# calculate the state of every station
stations <- AUS_state_locator(stations)
# inspect which states were sampled
table(stations$state)
```

## IBRA bioregion and subregion

The Interim Biogeographic Regionalisation for Australia 
([IBRA 7](https://www.dcceew.gov.au/environment/land/nrs/science/ibra)) divides the continent
into 89 bioregions and 419 subregions of similar climate, geology and vegetation. It is a 
common unit for pooling surveys and for reporting.

```{r ibra}
# calculate the bioregion and subregion of every station
stations <- ibra_classification(stations, lat_col = "latitude", long_col = "longitude")
# view bioregion
table(stations$IBRAbioRegionName)
# and subregions
table(stations$IBRAsubRegionName)
```

## Protected areas

WildObs `locationName` values are defined using the spatial hierarchy described above. 
Two functions are used to check sampling locations against the Collaborative Australian 
Protected Areas Database ([CAPAD 2022](https://www.dcceew.gov.au/environment/land/nrs/science/capad)).
`locationName_verification_CAPAD()` names the protected area each camera is in, or the
nearest one and the distance to it in metres. `locationName_buffer_CAPAD()` draws a buffer 
around each camera, merges buffers that overlap into one landscape, and names each landscape 
after the protected area that covers most of it, which groups nearby cameras into the same unit.

```{r capad}
# select a few stations from each project, to keep the example quick
few <- stations[stations$locationID %in% c("CFRAG_01_WildObsID_0001", "CFRAG_08_WildObsID_0001",
                                           "8_WildObsID_0010", "33_WildObsID_0010"), ]

# calculate the protected area each camera is in, or nearest to, beside the recorded locationName
verified <- locationName_verification_CAPAD(few)
# inspect the results 
verified[, c("locationID", "locationName", "CAPADlocationName", "CAPADminDistance")]

# calculate cameras whose 1 km buffers overlap share a landscape, named by its main protected area
buffered <- locationName_buffer_CAPAD(few, buffer_size = 1000)
# inspect the results
buffered[, c("locationID", "CAPADlocationNameBuffer")]
```

A recorded `locationName` can differ from the CAPAD name for good reasons. WildObs data 
curation, along with data provider input, inspects each clustering to ensure `locationName`
represents one clear landscape name, even when it spans several reserves. For example, 
the two Wet Tropics cameras above sit in Crater Lakes and Curtain Fig National Parks, and 
their landscape is recorded as `Eacham_Curtain_Fig_NPs` since both national parks neighbour 
each other. A camera can also sit outside every reserve: Woomargama station 33 is about 2.6 
km from the nearest protected area, Woomargama State Conservation Area, while its landscape 
is recorded as the national park to better group several nearby cameras in a homogeneous protected 
area. Its 1 km buffer touches no reserve, so `locationName_buffer_CAPAD()` names that 
landscape after the nearest one it finds instead. Treat a difference as a prompt to look and 
potentially correct the output, not as an error.

## Metric coordinates

Distances and grids need coordinates in metres. `UTM_coord_generator()` projects each
camera into the Universal Transverse Mercator zone its longitude falls in, and returns the
zone with the coordinates.

```{r utm}
# calculate the UTM zone, easting (X) and northing (Y) in metres for every deployment
utm <- UTM_coord_generator(deps)
# inspect
head(utm)
```

## Spacing between cameras

`find_nearest_neighbor_distance()` gives the distance from each station to its nearest
neighbour. Camera spacing decides whether neighbouring stations can be treated as
independent sites for a species with a given home range, and which grid cell size suits a
pooled analysis.

```{r spacing}
# calculate the nearest other station to each station, and how far it is
nn <- find_nearest_neighbor_distance(deps)
# inspect summary stats of spacing (in metres)
summary(nn$distance)
```

```{r spacing-plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Histogram of distances in metres from each camera station to its nearest neighbour."}
hist(nn$distance, breaks = 30, main = "Distance to the nearest camera station",
     xlab = "Distance (m)", col = "darkgreen", border = "white")
```

## Data sources

The CAPAD 2022 terrestrial and IBRA 7 subregion layers ship with WildObsR as the datasets
`capad` and `ibra`, simplified for size. Both are © Commonwealth of Australia (Department of
Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water), licensed under Creative Commons
Attribution. State boundaries come from the `ozmaps` package.
